overview: The file consists of Department of State finding aids and a cross-reference sheet indexing 1940–1941 records on Japan’s strategically important chemical, fuel, metallurgical, and engineering industries. The listed papers concern Japanese gas companies and their production of coke and coal; a proposed Japanese purchase of Chilean iodine amid the freezing of Japanese funds; intelligence on the chemical industry; Mitsubishi’s creation of a chemical combine and plans to increase magnesium production; steel and aluminum output; conversion of an automobile plant to war-related production; and Japan’s capacity to manufacture high-octane gasoline. The surviving pages describe or point to the underlying reports, memoranda, correspondence, and telegrams rather than reproducing them.

subfiles.title: Department of State list of papers on Japanese industrial production, items 24–32
subfiles.about: An archival index summarizes 1941 papers on Japanese chemicals, fuels, metals, engineering production, strategic purchases, and industrial conversion.
subfiles.summary: Items 24 and 25 cover a Justice Department memorandum on Japanese gas companies’ production of coke and coal and a Hull memorandum concerning Japan’s desire to buy iodine held by a Chilean corporation. The latter also records discussion of frozen Japanese funds, Japanese expansion, Hitler, control of maritime commerce, and suspected Japanese government profiteering. Later entries index War Department and British material on Japan’s chemical industry and Harrison’s telegrams from Switzerland reporting German-press information about Mitsubishi’s new chemical combine, increased magnesium production, Japanese steel and aluminum output, and the conversion of an automobile plant to aviation-related and marine-engine production.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet on Japan’s manufacture of high-octane gasoline
subfiles.from: Department of State, Far Eastern Affairs (Maxwell M. Hamilton)
subfiles.about: The sheet directs researchers to a record of a conversation about whether Japan possessed factories and refineries capable of producing high-octane gasoline.
subfiles.summary: This sheet indexes a January 11, 1940 Department of State note on Japan’s ability to manufacture high-octane gasoline. It records a conversation between Congressman Hamilton Fish and Maxwell M. Hamilton concerning whether Japan had suitable factories and refineries. Researchers are referred to file 894.24/820 for the underlying record.

interest: The file is useful as a compact map of U.S. wartime intelligence interests in Japanese industrial capacity immediately before the Pacific War. It connects commercial commodities such as iodine with financial controls and broader fears about Japanese and German expansion, while also showing reliance on British correspondence, German technical reporting, and diplomatic telegrams from neutral Switzerland. Its references to magnesium, high-octane fuel, metals, chemical warfare intelligence, and factory conversion reveal which industrial capabilities American officials considered strategically significant, and the cross-reference numbers provide leads to related records elsewhere in the decimal file.
